To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
peripheral blood mononucleated cells from asthmatic individuals produce an IL-5-like protein, which stimulates eosinophil differentiation in vitro.
1) IL-5-like factor is produced in vitro by mononuclear cells derived from asthmatic individuals; and 2) the factor can induce differentiation and activation of human cord blood eosinophils.
peripheral blood mononucleocytes of asthmatic patients produce IL-5-like factors that induce the proliferation and differentiation to eosinophils of cord blood mononucleocyte cultures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of an eosino-phil differentiation factor in culture supenatants of MNCs from asthmatic subjects.
a new approach to the treatment of allergic asthma by the inhibition of eosinophil differentiation and proliferation.
the identification of an eosonophil differentiation factor in MNC culture supernant of asthmatics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IL-5 activity was present in unstimulated culture supernatants obtained form MNCs of asthmatics and that this activity was neutralized by anti IL-5 antibodies.

the eosinophils in the blood and tissues of asthmatics are not only the end products of a process that is initiated and controlled by the immune system but also are actively recruited by the eosinophilic chemotactic factors.
the eosinophilia in asthma is not a consequence of the increased eosinophil production in the bone marrow but a result of a prolonged eosinophil survival in the circulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we found that the IL-5 activity in the MNC culture supernant from asthmatics can be neutralized with anti-IL-4 and anti-IL-6 antibodies, and that the IL-4 and IL-6 are important factors for the production of the IL-5 in the MNCs from asthmatics.
the IL-5 like activity is produced by the MNCs of the asthmatics and this activity is not related to the allergen stimulation.
we have demonstrated that peripheral blood mononucleated cells from asthmatic patient can secrete a protein with eosinophil differentiation properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
eosinophils are not only involved in the pathogenesis of asthma but they are a major contributor to the inflammatory process.
eosinophilia in asthma is a result of increased eosinophil production.
IL-5 is produced in asthmatics and may be important in the production of eosinophlia.
